WPCRL No.708 of 2025  Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Sagar Kothari, learned counsel for petitioner.

2. Mr. Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, learned A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand/ respondent Nos.1 and 2.
3.

By means of the present writ petition, the petitioner has challenged the First Information Report No.0079 of 2025 dated 02.05.2025, for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 IPC,
lodged by respondent No.3 at P.S. Rajpur, District Dehradun.
4.

It was contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has falsely been implicated in the aforesaid FIR and though, he was named in the FIR, but there was no allegation against him.

5. It is further contended by him that the petitioner was authorized representative of the Company named as M/s. High Visions Multiplier Pvt. Ltd., who has to purchase some land at Dehradun and for the purpose of said purchase of land, an agreement to sale was executed between the Company ant sellers-Gopal Singh, Prem Singh and Shyam Singh, owners of the said land.

entities.text: M/s. High Visions Multiplier Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In part payment of the said agreement to sale, a sum of Rupees Forty Lakh was given to the owners of the land by the Company, out of which, Rupees Thirty Eight Lakh was paid through RTGS and Rupees Two Lakh was paid cash.
Subsequently, the sellers have not sold the land to Company, but sold the same to a third party.

6. It is also contended by him that the sellers of the said land have not named in the FIR and they have not made party while only the petitioner was named in the FIR.
7.

He further submits that in the entire transaction, no money was taken by the petitioner and there was even no entrustment of money to the petitioner; all transactions were done by the Company straightway in favour of the sellers of the land.

1 8.

After hearing the learned counsel for the petitioner, this Court had directed learned State Counsel to bring on record the role which has been assigned to the petitioner after the investigation till date.

9. Today, learned State Counsel has passed on to this Court written instruction dated 10.07.2025,
which is taken on record.

On the basis of said instruction, learned State Counsel submits that the petitioner got the land sold in favour of the third person, who are not party to the agreement to sale and this is how he defrauded the company.

10. Having heard the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court is of the view that prima-facie, no case is made out against the petitioner in the aforesaid Sections on the basis of the aforesaid facts.

11. Issue notice to respondent No.3, returnable within six weeks.
12.
Steps to be taken within 03 days.
Meanwhile, respondents may file counter affidavit(s).
15. Interim order dated 07.07.2025 is extended till the next date of listing, provided the petitioner cooperates with the investigation.
16. Stay Application (IA/1/2025) stands disposed of.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
